transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2029-12-03
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Santos (Redwood SE), Ivy Chen (Redwood SC); Aisha Patel (Citrine Head of Search), Tom Nguyen (Citrine ML Eng), Priya Rao (Citrine Security)

Auto-generated summary (auto):
Citrine is evaluating where to host embeddings and rerank -- hosted API vs dedicated reserved capacity vs private VPC/on-prem. Main concerns: throughput at 500+ qps for 512-dim embeddings, tail latency for fanout + rerank, data residency and SOC2/compliance, cost tradeoffs and fallback routing for partial outages. They run a hybrid search + rerank pipeline with a vector DB (open-source VDB) and want clarity on where Redwood fits (embedding generation vs rerank model hosting vs combined).

Topics covered:
- current infra and vector DB (self-hosted Milvus / custom vector store)
- throughput targets and typical workload shape (spiky, peak 1k qps for flash sales)
- embedding dimensionality (512 -> exploring 256 compact embeddings)
- rerank latency budget (75-120ms p95) and batching strategies
- hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
- security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, region limits

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Lena, AE on the Search/Embeddings team at Redwood. Marco and Ivy from our side too. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha Patel: Hey thanks, doing well. Excited to dig in. We tried a couple of quick notes — hopefully we can get through hosting options and a throughput sketch.
[00:15] Marco Santos: Great. Real quick agenda: 1) understand current pipeline and success metrics, 2) discuss hosting options and tradeoffs, 3) next steps and PO C scoping. Sound good?
[00:25] Tom Nguyen: Yeah that's perfect. I'll be the technical person — I run their embed pipeline and orchestrate the VDB.
[00:29] Priya Rao: I'll jump in on security questions. We have strict region and KMS needs.
[00:33] Lena Park: Awesome. Aisha, could you share high-level what you're running today for retrieval and rerank?
[00:39] Aisha Patel: Sure. We have a hybrid approach — open-source vector store (Milvus/our fork) for initial recall, then a lightweight transformer reranker for top-100 that we host in Kubernetes on EKS. Embeddings are 512 dims from an internal model. We also store user signals and product metadata in Postgres.
[00:54] Tom Nguyen: To add, our p99 for the rerank step is...uh... we're seeing 300 to 600ms right now under load, so it's not great. We need p95 < 120ms ideally. Avg QPS daily is 150-200, but during promotions it spikes to 800-1,000 for 10-20 minute windows.
[01:15] Marco Santos: Got it, spiky workload with tight tail-latency needs for rerank. Are you mostly doing embedding generation at request time or precompute?
[01:22] Aisha Patel: Mix. For freshness we have some on-the-fly gens, but most product embeddings are precomputed and written to the VDB. The challenge is when we need to re-rank with user context, that's often live.
[01:34] Ivy Chen: That helps. For the live rerank, are you doing full-context L2 or dot-product, and what's the current fanout to embeddings before rerank?
[01:42] Tom Nguyen: Fanout is typically top-100, sometimes top-300 for some categories. Similarity is cosine/dot. The reranker uses a small cross-attention model, about 250M params.
[01:52] Lena Park: Ok. One of the tradeoffs we usually discuss is where to run the reranker — in Redwood hosted vs Redwood dedicated (reserved GPUs) vs customer private (VPC). For spiky loads with tight p95, dedicated gives predictable throughput; hosted is easier to spin up but if you need strict tail-latency it can be variable unless you use reserved capacity.
[02:12] Priya Rao: Security-wise, we need SOC2, SaaS data segmentation, and KMS for keys. We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Can Hosted meet that?
[02:22] Marco Santos: Hosted can meet many of those — we have SOC2 and provide audit logs and KMS integrations. For the strictest controls, Private (VPC) gives you control plane isolation and customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated is a middle ground: reserved capacity in our infra but logical isolation and region pinning.
[02:36] Aisha Patel: Cost is also big. If we go dedicated it's a big commitment but might save cost during peaks. Do you have a simple cost example for 100M tokens/month plus 500 qps embedding/rerank?
[02:46] Lena Park: We'll send a sample TCO. Off the cuff, dedicated can be 20-40% cheaper for heavy steady usage, but spikes still matter — we can enable burst capacity. Hosted has per-token and per-embedding pricing that is easier to start with.
[02:58] Tom Nguyen: On vector DB integration: do you recommend we keep embeddings in our Milvus or push them to a managed Redis/FAISS? We want minimal latency on the recall step.
[03:07] Marco Santos: No single right answer. If you're tied to Milvus already, we work with client-side vector stores. Redwood typically sits as the inference layer (embedding generation + rerank) and you keep the VDB. For lower latency recall, some customers use an in-memory FAISS or ANN cache in front of Milvus; others go multi-tier with an edge cache.
[03:24] Aisha Patel: For rerank quantization — have you tested 8-bit quantized rerankers with preserved quality? We are sensitive about relevance loss.
[03:30] Marco Santos: Yes — we have internal benchmarks and model-specific guidance. For many rerank models, 8-bit or mixed quant can preserve quality with small delta; we recommend running an eval dataset. We'll share our quantization playbook and some sample eval metrics.
[03:44] Tom Nguyen: Great. Could you also share kernel/compile details? We saw on your docs mention of kernel selection based on seq length — our reranker has variable context lengths 128-512.
[03:52] Ivy Chen: Absolutely. Our runtime picks kernels based on model arch and sequence length distributions; for cross-attention-heavy rerankers the KV-cache and attention kernels matter. We'll include high-level notes on what tends to perform for 128 vs 512 seq.
[04:04] Priya Rao: A question on private deploy: if we do VPC, can Redwood's control plane still see customer configs? We need to know about metadata leakage.
[04:12] Marco Santos: In Private deployments, the control plane is logically separated; telemetry can be sent to your account but models and tokens are within your VPC. For the on-prem option, the control plane can be customer-run and logs remain internal. We'll share the security architecture doc.
[04:26] Aisha Patel: On fallback/resilience: suppose a dedicated cluster goes down during peak — how do you route to hosted fallback without double-billing or performance surprises?
[04:36] Lena Park: We have smart routing policies: failover can route to compatible model variants in hosted with throttles. Billing is per-request destination, and we can set policies to limit blowout spend (e.g., cap fallback throughput or use a cheaper small model for degraded mode). We'll send an example policy snippet.
[04:53] Tom Nguyen: For our numbers: we care about p95 < 120ms for rerank. What's realistic if we keep rerank in Redwood dedicated with a 250M param model and batched top-100 across 16 requests?
[05:05] Marco Santos: Hard to say without exact fanout and batching window. In many benchmarks, a batched rerank on a 80GB GPU with continuous batching and 16-32 batch size can hit p95 ~60-90ms for 250M models for top-100. But spikes reduce batching efficiency; that's where tail starts to climb.
[05:23] Aisha Patel: We also need embedding dimensionality guidance. If we move from 512 to 256 dims to save storage, what hit to relevance should we expect?
[05:31] Ivy Chen: It depends heavily on dataset. Some customers see negligible drop moving 512->256 with a small retrieval loss but big storage/throughput gains. We recommend an A/B on a holdout. We can help run a small-dim sweep with your sample corpus.
[05:44] Priya Rao: Regarding compliance, we need access controls at token level and audit for operations team. Do you have RBAC and SSO integrations?
[05:51] Marco Santos: Yes — RBAC, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and token-scoped policies are supported. We'll provide the enterprise security packet link.
[06:00] Tom Nguyen: Ok last technical — what's the pattern for multi-region failover for VDB and rerank? If recall is in region A but rerank in region B, latency is bad.
[06:09] Lena Park: Ideally co-locate rerank near VDB to reduce cross-region hops. Smart routing can prefer same-region model pools; otherwise you pay for the latency penalty. For global apps, many customers run regional dedicated pools.
[06:22] Aisha Patel: This has been great. Quick recap and next steps?
[06:26] Lena Park: Sure. Recap: Citrine needs: 1) p95 < 120ms for rerank at spikes, 2) cost estimate for 100M tokens/mo and 500-1k peak qps, 3) security packet and SOC2, 4) quantization/playbook and a small dim-sweep. Next steps — we'll send pricing, security docs, and schedule the quantization deep-dive with Tom.
[06:45] Priya Rao: I'll send our compliance checklist by Friday.
[06:47] Lena Park: Great — we'll get those items out. Thanks everyone.
